family: Estructuras Pretensa 'Viga VI' bridge I-beams and VPI-45 juxtaposed beam
source_status: producer brochure (undated); outline estimated from schematic

locators.VI: PDF p1: 'Vigas VI + prelosas' schematic and table (Peso propio kg/m, Altura m, Luz máxima)
locators.VPI-45: PDF p2: 'Vigas VI45 yuxtapuestas' schematic (0.45 dimensioned) and table

geometry_notes: ESTIMATE (all sizes). The brochure prints only depth, self-weight and spans. Outline shape (plain I: top flange with a short taper to the web, bottom bulb with a taper, equal top and bottom widths as drawn) is taken from the PDF p1 schematic, rendered at 500 dpi and measured by pixel run-lengths.

VI schematic assumed drawn at the maximum 1.60 m depth (its dimension reads 'Altura de viga Mín.=0.90 Máx.=1.60'). Measured at that scale and rounded to 5 mm: flange widths 585, top flange 110, top taper 45, web ~140, bottom taper 120, bottom flange 230 mm. Unfitted, that outline gives 0.412 m2 = 1030 kg/m at 2500 kg/m3 vs published 948 kg/m (+8.6%), supporting the scale assumption.

CONVENTION: for each VI type the four flange heights are scaled by depth/1600, flange widths held at 585 mm, and the web width solved so the gross area equals published kg/m / 2500 kg/m3. Held-width/fixed-flange and uniformly scaled templates were rejected: the published masses are not linear in depth (e.g. VI-154 864 kg/m vs VI-130 811), so flange proportions must vary between moulds.

Fitted webs: VI-90 116, VI-100 145, VI-120 124, VI-130 129, VI-154 95, VI-160 112 mm. The non-monotonic webs reflect the tabulated masses, not a producer rule; treat every dimension as uncertain by at least +/-20%.

VPI-45: scaled from the PDF p2 schematic using its printed 0.45 m depth (591 px/m at 600 dpi): width 415, top flange 70, top taper 50, bottom taper 100, bottom flange 95, web ~95 mm (measured). Web solved to 296 kg/m at 2500 kg/m3 (measured-web outline is +1.0% heavier). The deck shows these beams side by side with the in-situ slab; width 415 mm is the module.
No section properties published; the only validation is self-weight, which is enforced by construction.
